records.text:
Ultrasonography: Revealed a multilocular cyst with septa attached to the testis without testicular abnormalities.
MRI Findings:  Image Title: Pre-operative magnetic resonance Images (MRI)  Image Description: Showed fluid-filled sac (7 cm) and multinodal cyst without solid lesion. No contrast enhanced rim on the cyst. Contents showed high-intensity on T1-weighted image and relatively low-intensity on T1-weighted image consistent with hematoma.

records.query: Need the serum tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) that were requested but not yet returned; the ultrasound/MRI showing a multilocular cystic hematoma without solid lesion or testicular abnormality makes malignancy unlikely, but these markers are essential to definitively rule out a hemorrhagic germ cell tumor.

bindings.label: Right scrotal swelling rapidly growing over 3 months without local pain
Patient is a 50-year-old Japanese man, non-smoker, with medical history of hypertension treated with ARB tablet daily and no known allergies
He underwent a puncture at a prior hospital where red-colored fluid was found
No history of trauma or infections including STDs
Physical examination of the scrotum revealed swelling on the right side
Ultrasound and MRI show a multilocular cystic lesion attached to the testis without solid components, contrast enhancement, or testicular abnormality
Pathological examination shows bland tall columnar cells with no stromal invasion in the cyst wall
Immunohistochemistry is positive for EpCAM/BerEP4, negative for calretinin, and positive for ER/PR
MRI shows T1-hyperintense contents within the multilocular cystic lesion
Serum tumor marker results are not yet available
Benign multilocular paratesticular cystic lesion (mesothelial/epithelial origin) with hemorrhage
